5 questions. Click an answer to check it: you will see right away whether it is correct, with a short explanation. Nothing is saved.

::: {.sb-quiz-q data-answer="0"}
**1.** $A$ is 3×3 and $B$ is 3×2. What is the shape of `A @ B`?

::: {.sb-quiz-options}
- 3×2
- 3×3
- 2×3
- It is not defined
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-explain}
An $m \times n$ matrix times an $n \times p$ matrix gives an $m \times p$ matrix: here 3×2.
:::
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-q data-answer="2"}
**2.** And `B @ A` (3×2 times 3×3)?

::: {.sb-quiz-options}
- 3×3
- 2×2
- It gives an error: the inner dimensions (2 and 3) do not match
- The same as `A @ B`
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-explain}
The number of **columns** of the first matrix must equal the number of **rows** of the second one.
:::
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-q data-answer="1"}
**3.** $P = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2\\ 3 & 4\end{bmatrix}$, $Q = \begin{bmatrix}5 & 6\\ 7 & 8\end{bmatrix}$. What is the element in the first row, second column of $PQ$?

::: {.sb-quiz-options}
- 12
- 22
- 19
- 50
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-explain}
It is the dot product of row 1 of $P$ and column 2 of $Q$: $1 \times 6 + 2 \times 8 = 22$.
:::
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-q data-answer="1"}
**4.** `x = np.array([1, -2, -5])` and `y = np.array([4, 3, -1])`. What does `np.matmul(x, y)` return?

::: {.sb-quiz-options}
- An error: two 3×1 matrices cannot be multiplied
- `3`, the dot product
- `[4, -6, 5]`
- A 3×3 matrix
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-explain}
For two 1-D arrays NumPy computes the dot product: $4 - 6 + 5 = 3$. With `reshape((3, 1))` on both, you would get an error.
:::
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-q data-answer="1"}
**5.** What does `A - 2` do when $A$ is a 3×3 array?

::: {.sb-quiz-options}
- It gives an error: you cannot subtract a number from a matrix
- It subtracts 2 from every element (broadcasting)
- It subtracts 2 from the diagonal only
- It removes the last 2 rows
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-explain}
Mathematically this is not defined, but NumPy **broadcasts** the scalar to a 3×3 array and subtracts element by element.
:::
:::
